To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

exposure to cigarette smoke induces an asthma-like disease in mice, and that this disease is accompanied by an increase in the number of tDCs and a decrease in the number of Treg cells, both in the lung and in the spleen, and that the tDCs have an immunosuppressive effect on T cells, and that Treg cells have an immunosurpresssive effect on T cells.

cigarette smoke exposure increases the number of CD4+CD25+FoxP3+ Treg cells and the suppressive function of Treg cells in the lungs of mice with asthma, and the increased number and suppressive function of lung Treg cells in cigarette-smoke-exposed mice is related to the increased severity of airway inflammation and airway hyperresponsiveness.
cigarette smoke exposure (CSE) in a mouse model with allergic airway disease results in increased numbers of tDCs in the airway, which are capable of inducing Treg cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of smoking on the development and progression of allergic asthma.
the role of the immune system in the pathogenesis of asthma.
the effects of cigarette smoke exposure on the immune system of the lungs, particularly on the counts and function of tDC and CD4+ Treg cells in an asthma mouse model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cigarette smoke exposure can induce the differentiation of Treg and Treg cells, which in turn can suppress the differentiation of Th17 cells, thereby inhibiting the development of airway inflammation.
cigarette smoke exposure has an effect on the counts and function of tDC and regulatory T cells in a mouse asthma model.
cigarette smoke (CS) exposure exacerbates the development of allergic asthma and that CS exposure may be a risk factor for the development of allergic airway diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cigarette smoke exposure (CSE) in the mouse model of allergic asthma can induce the increase of the counts and functions for Treg and tDC cells.
we have demonstrated a novel mechanism by which cigarette smoke (CS) exposure induces airway inflammation in a mouse model.

we demonstrated the potential of using a mouse model to investigate the effects of cigarette smoke on the development of asthma and to investigate the role of tDCs and Treg cells on the development of cigarette smoke-induced asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cigarette smoke exposure in mice with allergic asthma exacerbates airway inflammation and airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR).
exposure to cigarette smoke can alter the counts and functions  of tDCs and Tregs in a mouse model  of asthma
cigarette smoke exposure can alter the balance between regulatory and effector T cells in the lungs of mice with allergic asthma.
